descriptionPlain:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.
 
That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.
 
Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.
 
One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.
 
That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.
 
If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.
We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

lists.content:
• Run repeatable recording sessions on football pitches and in controlled environments using provided test protocols
  • Capture logs, photos and reference video, and verify that recording data reaches the cloud
  • Document every test session, review recordings for defects and clearly flag issues
  • Support internal chamber, bench and long-running endurance tests
  • Help with communications for our Alpha and Beta test programmes
  • Facilitate first-time-user sessions with non-expert participants and collect feedback
  • Prepare, charge, label and track test cameras and accessories
  • After the project gate, verify pilot and early-production units, regression-test production builds and record real matches as the Nordic season restarts

• You are currently enrolled in a relevant higher-education programme and based in Copenhagen, Denmark
  • You can work reliably and independently while following detailed instructions
  • You have a structured approach and strong attention to detail
  • You are fluent in english and can communicate observations clearly in writing and in person
  • You are comfortable handling technical equipment and learning new tools
  • You are willing to work outdoors on football pitches as well as in controlled test environments
  • An interest in sports, cameras, hardware or software testing is an advantage, but not required

lists.content:
• Execute and shape the go-to-market strategy for Australia and New Zealand, and own the budget and spend behind it.

  • Own Veo's relationships with key football and rugby partners across the region: leagues, federations, associations and governing bodies. Renewals, day-to-day contact, and finding ways to deepen partnerships over time.

  • Build new partnerships at national and state level, leading from first conversation through to signed contract and long-term execution.

  • Drive market activations with partners, including events, seminars, workshops, campaigns, that build Veo's presence on the ground and convert partner reach into real growth.

  • Hit ARR and revenue targets through partner activations and sales enablement, including running presentations with partners to their clubs and members.

  • Map partner organisations and understand how decisions actually get made, so relationships sit with the right people.

  • Travel to tournaments, conventions and partner sites across Australia and New Zealand. Face-time matters.

  • Feed market intelligence back to HQ. What you hear on the ground shapes how our product and leadership teams in Copenhagen make decisions.

  • Use AI to move faster and work smarter: better prep, sharper outreach, cleaner reporting.

  • Report clearly on pipeline, partner performance, and key metrics.

• 3+ years in partner account management, partnerships, sales or marketing. Sports, sports-tech background preferred.

  • A deep understanding of the football and rugby codes in Australia and New Zealand, and a real network within them. You know how associations and governing bodies make decisions, and you know people inside them.

  • A track record of both closing deals and managing long-term partner relationships, not just one or the other.

  • Experience activating partnerships in the field. You know how to turn a signed contract into something that drives adoption at grassroots level.

  • Great with people, structured in how you work, and ideally experienced with project management.

  • Someone who uses AI as a genuine work tool. Not a buzzword; you know how to use different AI tools to be more efficient, have a high output, and solve problems.

  • Comfortable working autonomously. You will clearly advocate for your market, communicate across time zones, and know when to escalate.

  • Excellent written and spoken English.

  • Currently living in a well-connected area of Australia. (Sydney, Melbourne, or Brisbane preferred)

• Full ownership of a market with room to grow: your own region, your own region, your own partners, your own budget, with a global team of colleagues in Europe and the USA to learn from, and a direct line to the Global Director of Partnerships.

  • A product people in sport actually want, which makes the partnership work a lot easier.

  • Autonomy and the freedom to find your own approach.

  • A flat, international organisation that moves fast and does not waste your time with unnecessary processes. You will work closely with your market and visit us in Copenhagen.

You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

lists.content:
• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

  • Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

  • Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

  • Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

  • Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

  • Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

  • Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

  • Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

  • Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

  • Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

  • Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

  • Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

  • Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

  • Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

  • Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

  • Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

  • An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

  • Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

  • A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

  • Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

  • Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

  • Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

lists.content:
You'll join the Security Enablement Team and focus on the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership of the team's work, pair on complex problems, and rotate responsibilities. The systems themselves stay with the owning teams, and our job is to make those teams successful.

  • Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for our office and data center networks and the VPN that connects them, as part of the network security direction the team sets together. Day-to-day operation and firewall changes stay with the team that owns the network
  • Build patterns and tooling for secure cross-site connectivity and endpoint security posture that IT can adopt and run, in a way that supports how Veo engineers actually work
  • Build the patterns and automation for workforce identity and access, including SSO hygiene, MFA enforcement for employees, and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows for access to product systems, with IT owning the day-to-day operation
  • Build automated checks that surface drift in cloud configuration and network rules, so the owning teams get a signal and can act on it
  • Act on infrastructure and network findings from external penetration tests, routed through the team's shared intake, with the owning teams driving remediation
  • Build the first version of cross-cutting capabilities, such as the cross-site VPN or the drift checks, then hand each one to a long-term owner with a written transition that covers the runbook, ownership, and escalation path
  • Partner with GRC to build evidence pipelines for IT and access-related controls that produce auditable output without manual follow-up
  • Run office hours where IT, platform, and product teams can get a network or access review

    • As the team matures, you'll help shape how Veo's network and identity stack evolves across our offices and clouds as the company grows.

This role deliberately sits where IT, cloud, and security meet. You do not need to be world class at all three. You are strong in one or two and comfortable operating across the rest.

You likely have several years of experience at that intersection. That tends to show up in several of the following:

  • Solid IT fundamentals: networking, identity, endpoint posture, MFA, and SSO at production scale
  • Cloud infrastructure experience: hands-on work on at least one of GCP or AWS, including IAM, networking, and basic Terraform-style IaC
  • Workforce identity and access: hands-on experience with SSO and identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace) and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows
  • A security mindset layered on that IT and cloud depth: you instinctively look for misconfigurations, drift, and bad access patterns, without needing to be a dedicated security specialist
  • Cross-context comfort: you can work on an office network problem and a product cloud problem in the same week without context-switching pain
  • Platform-as-product mindset: you've built internal tooling that real teams adopt, with guard rails built into the tools people already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured impact
  • Comfort handing work back to a long-term owner once the build phase is done
  • Collaboration: you work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively, and write things down.
    • Nice to have: VPN solutions at scale (Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, WireGuard), endpoint management tooling, and audit log pipelines.

You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on most of it but not all of it, apply anyway. People who span IT, cloud, and security are rare, and we do not expect every box ticked. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

lists.content:
You'll join the platform engineering team that owns these areas together. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities.

  • Evolve KickOff (our GitOps platform) to improve developer experience.
  • Support service migrations to KickOff, partnering with product teams.
  • Maintain and optimize KickOff on AWS EKS.
  • Manage our on-premises Kubernetes clusters running ML training workloads.
  • Establish monitoring, alerting, and observability using LGTM.
  • Debug distributed systems spanning multiple environments.
  • Create documentation and tooling that makes infrastructure approachable

    • As the platform matures, you'll have opportunities to shape multi-cluster architecture, GPU workload scheduling, disaster recovery strategy, and cloud provider independence.

We're looking for someone with 3-5 years running production infrastructure, including:
 
  • Production Kubernetes: You've operated K8s in production and understand the operational reality, not just tutorials.
  • Platform-as-product mindset: You've built internal tooling that real teams use, gathered feedback, and measured impact on productivity.
  • Infrastructure as Code: Strong Terraform, Crossplane, or similar experience.
  • Observability: You've implemented monitoring and alerting that helps teams operate confidently.
  • Security awareness: You know how to embed security into platform design without slowing teams down.
  • Problem-solving: You debug complex distributed systems and design practical solutions.
  • Collaboration: You work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively.

    • Nice to have: GitOps tools (Flux, ArgoCD), Cilium, multi-cloud architecture, on-prem K8s experience.

You’ll join a Copenhagen-based platform team of 5 engineers with shared ownership of KickOff and our on-prem Kubernetes clusters. We work closely together day to day through pairing, code reviews, and a rotating ownership model for operational responsibilities and platform improvements.

You’ll collaborate regularly with the Processing Platform team on workload needs, reliability, and developer experience, and you’ll use feedback from product and engineering teams to shape platform priorities and improve how teams build and ship on KickOff.

We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

Veo is a global leader in AI-based sports camera technology. Our innovative, fully automatic camera solution enables sports teams to record matches and training sessions without a camera operator. We’re democratizing the world of sports by granting video analysis for teams on all levels—a privilege that used to be only for the few. But what truly sets us apart? Our people. We’re a diverse group of innovative thinkers, creators, and problem-solvers who believe in delivering an incredible product—and having fun while doing it.


The Opportunity
Veo's Revenue Platform is the engine that drives the business. Each subscription, order, invoice, payment and shipment passes through the platform that our team built. We are looking for a senior engineer to help take it to the next level. 
The team owns the core revenue engine that sits between Veo's products and the systems that run the business: billing, payments, CRM, ERP and fulfillment. Other teams use our APIs to sell, quote, bill and provision. Finance relies on us to get the numbers right.
The foundations are in place. The next chapter is about making the platform more robust, easier to build on, and ready for new markets, products and pricing models. You'll model subscription lifecycles, amendments, quotes, tax and payment flows. You'll make workflows stay correct when a third-party API fails halfway through an order. You'll also work closely with Finance, Sales and Product so the business logic in code matches how the business actually works.

lists.content:

  • Build and maintain integrations with cloud services, including REST APIs, OpenTelemetry, and AWS S3.
  • Implement wireless communication features using BLE and Wi-Fi for connectivity with mobile devices.
  • Develop and maintain application-layer protocols, including GATT services, Protobuf-based communication, and data serialization.
  • Collaborate closely with AI, video processing, and cloud teams to support the broader camera platform.

  • Experience integrating embedded systems with cloud services such as REST APIs, OpenTelemetry, and AWS S3, including debugging and operational troubleshooting.
  • Experience building applications that integrate BLE and Wi-Fi, including GATT services, connection management, Protobuf-based protocols, and communication with mobile devices.

  • RTOS: Zephyr

lists.content:
• Make the case before the spec. Every hardware programme starts with a written argument - problem, user, willingness to pay - that has to hold up before anyone cuts metal.

  • Choose what belongs in the line. Decide what each product is for, what it deliberately isn't, and how they ladder - including saying no to good ideas that haven't earned a slot.

  • Turn cameras into products. A camera that records is a device; one that tells a coach something at halftime is a product. You own that seam across hardware, AI and app - and you own the launch.

  • Put a number on it. Price, positioning, margin, attach, and the subscription revenue the device unlocks. A camera earns its place by what it's worth, not by what it can do.

  • Aim while aiming is still cheap. Bring optics, thermal, battery and cost into the decision early, when a change costs a conversation rather than a year.

  • Prove we aimed right. Define what success means - activation, sessions recorded, field reliability, retention - and report it straight, including when it isn't working.

• Proven product management experience bringing physical hardware products to market, where hardware and software meet.
  • A track record of choosing a direction and defending it - arguing for value, not gathering requirements. You can kill a good idea because it doesn't pay for itself.
  • Commercial instinct, and evidence of getting genuinely close to users.
  • Comfort committing on incomplete information. Hardware allows no fast follow, so the call has to be made early and made well.
  • Fluency in optics, thermals, battery and cost to have a real conversation with engineers.
  • Bonus: hardware-plus-subscription business models, consumer electronics and DFM exposure, or a sports background.

lists.content:
You will join a focused platform security team and operate as its most senior engineer. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities, and we expect this role to set the bar.

  • Design and build the paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, and CVE response, running inside the pipelines teams already use, with findings routed to the owners who can fix them under tracked SLAs
  • Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for a unified internal network and VPN across GCP, AWS, and our Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen offices, while the team that owns the network keeps running it
  • Work with the auth service maintainers on identity and access, including MFA rollouts, removal of shared accounts, and cleanup of long-lived tokens, so the patterns stay theirs to own
  • Make workload identity the paved road for CI/CD, using OIDC between GitHub Actions and AWS or GCP, packaged so teams can migrate themselves
  • Build audit logging as a shared capability that teams plug into rather than reinvent
  • Turn GRC controls into technical implementations, with evidence pipelines that produce auditable output without manual follow-up
  • Own the contracting cycle for external penetration tests and build the intake, classification, and tracking system that routes findings to named owners, while the owning teams remediate
  • Hand each capability off cleanly, with a runbook, a named owner, and an escalation path, and run office hours where product and platform teams can get a security review or a paved-road question answered
  • Mentor the rest of the team and raise the security bar across Builders

    • As the team matures, you will help shape our multi-environment network architecture, our identity and access patterns, and the long-term security posture of the product.

This is a deliberately merged platform security and identity role. You do not need to be world class at both. You likely have several years of production infrastructure and security experience behind you, and you are deep and credible in one of these areas and ready to grow into the other.

That depth tends to show up in several of the following:

  • Platform security: you have run vulnerability scanning, CVE management, and image scanning at scale, and you know the operational reality of getting CVEs fixed, beyond standing up the tooling
  • Identity and auth: you have worked hands-on inside an auth codebase, rolled out MFA on live systems, and managed token lifecycles in CI/CD with OIDC and workload identity
  • Network security at scale: you have designed and run a unified internal network across multiple cloud providers and offices, with a VPN approach that holds up
  • Platform-as-product mindset: you have built internal security tooling that other teams chose to adopt, with guard rails built into the tools developers already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured the impact
  • Infrastructure as Code: strong experience with Terraform, Crossplane, or similar

    • Nice to have: GitOps tools such as Flux or ArgoCD, Cilium, Kubernetes security at scale, and experience building security into a GRC evidence pipeline.

You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. This role sets the technical direction for the team's quarterly missions. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on three or four items but not all of them, apply anyway. The "deep in one, ready to grow into the other" framing above is not a hedge, it is how we actually hire at this level. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

• Own the partnership strategy for basketball and shape it for field hockey and baseball, mapping each sport’s landscape (governing bodies, leagues, circuits, tournament operators, and influential clubs) and prioritizing where Veo can win.

  • Land and grow organization-level partnerships. Identify, pitch, negotiate, and close agreements with leagues, associations, and federations that embed Veo across their member clubs and teams.

  • Drive adoption inside partner organizations through programs like video compliance (for example, leagues that require member teams to record their games), league-wide recording, and content and data solutions that give partners a reason to make Veo part of their operations.

  • Own the full partner lifecycle: onboarding, training, support, co-marketing, renewals, and long-term growth, serving as the main point of contact for your partners.

  • Build and test new go-to-market motions. Run pilots, starting in basketball, learn what works, and turn early wins into repeatable, scalable programs.

  • Work hand in hand with Sales and Marketing to turn partnerships into pipeline, supplying sales teams with targeted resources, partner-specific offers, and co-marketing campaigns.

  • Represent Veo in person at tournaments, showcases, conferences, and league events, and demo the product to coaches, athletic directors, and organizers.

  • Amplify each sport’s story by curating featured content and working with the social team to grow Veo’s visibility in each community.

  • Measure and report what matters: partner-sourced revenue, camera and club adoption within partner organizations, pipeline, renewals, and community engagement.

• Partnership Builder: You know how to open doors at the organizational level, build trust with decision-makers, and negotiate agreements that work for both sides.

  • Scaler & Pioneer: You enjoy doubling down on proven approaches and also blazing a trail in sports where Veo has less awareness.

  • Strategic Operator: You can turn a partnership into measurable adoption and revenue, and you’re comfortable owning a plan, a number, and a calendar.

  • Community Catalyst: You energize coaches, athletes, and organizers, and you turn enthusiasm into advocacy.

  • Competitive Closer: Basketball is a crowded market, and coaches expect a high-touch experience. You stay responsive, earn their trust, and win them over against established competitors.

• 3–5 years of experience in partnership management, business development, or market development, ideally in sports, sports tech, or another high-growth industry.

  • A deep knowledge of the U.S. basketball landscape (club and travel circuits, high school and collegiate pathways, governing bodies). An existing basketball network is a big plus, and familiarity with field hockey or baseball is a bonus.

  • A track record of forming and growing partnerships with leagues, associations, or similar organizations.

  • Strong skills in strategy, project management, and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently with colleagues in Miami and at our Copenhagen HQ.

  • Willingness and ability to travel 30–40% of the time, with peak travel around key tournament and event seasons (often weekends in spring and summer).

  • Authorization to work in the U.S.

• An international team of skilled, relatable colleagues in a flat organization.

  • The freedom to shape your own path and solve real problems your way.

  • Work that genuinely contributes to the future of sports.

  • U.S. benefits: health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k), PTO.

  • Perks like fitness, phone, and internet subsidies.

  • A lively environment where no two days are the same and your ideas matter.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

 

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

 

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.


The role

You'll be the person who takes a video from idea to finished file — on your own.

 

Say we need a product walkthrough of a new Veo feature. Here's what that looks like for you:

 

  1. Plan: Set the shoot date and book the product designer who built the feature.

  2. Find the story: Interview them and write the script.

  3. Set up: Light and frame the set.

  4. Shoot: Run the shoot on our two Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6Ks and direct the person on camera.

  5. Finish: Edit, grade, mix, subtitle, and export every format we need.

 

Nobody hands you a shot list. Nobody needs to check in halfway.

 

You'll also use AI throughout your work. Some shots you'll generate in tools like Higgsfield instead of filming them. Some steps — transcripts, rough cuts, subtitles, versioning — you'll hand to AI so you can spend your time on the parts that need your eye.

 

You'll join Veo's Owned & Creative team in Copenhagen, working alongside graphic designers, a video producer focused on AI-generated ads, and the wider marketing team.

What you'll do

Own production end-to-end

 

  • Take a brief (or spot the need yourself) and turn it into a production plan: concept, timeline, locations, people, and gear.

  • Plan and book shoot dates with colleagues across Veo, from product designers to coaches and community members.

  • Research the topic and interview subject-matter experts to find the story worth telling.

  • Write scripts, talking points, and storyboards.

 

Run the shoot

 

  • Set up the set: lighting, sound, framing, and camera settings.

  • Operate our 2× Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6K setup, including multi-camera interviews and B-roll.

  • Direct and interview people on camera — most of them aren't actors — so they come across confident and natural, and stick to the script when they need to.

  • Shoot on location, in studio, and out on the pitch.

 

Finish the video

 

  • Edit in DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro: story, pacing, color grading, sound mix, graphics, subtitles, and CTAs.

  • Deliver multi-format versions for paid social (Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Instagram), YouTube, veo.co, and email.

  • Organize and archive footage and finished assets in our DAM (Frontify) so the whole team can find and reuse them.

 

Make AI part of how you work

 

  • Generate shots, B-roll, and scenes with AI video tools such as Higgsfield, and blend them with live-action footage.

  • Use AI to speed up your workflow — automated transcripts and rough cuts, text-based editing, AI subtitles, script drafts, and fast versioning for different markets and formats.

  • Keep testing new tools and share what works with the team.

 

Work with the team — without needing to be managed

 

  • Align with graphic designers on art direction and brand, and with marketers on campaign goals.

  • Manage your own pipeline, priorities, and deadlines, and flag trade-offs early.

  • Brief and coordinate freelancers (photographers, extra crew) when a project needs them.

• A portfolio that shows videos you've taken from idea to final cut — ideally including interview-led or product content. Please tell us what you did on each piece.

  • 3+ years of hands-on video production experience, in-house, at an agency, or freelance.

  • Strong camera skills — confident with cinema cameras (Blackmagic experience is a plus), lighting, and recording clean audio.

  • Strong editing skills in DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro, including color grading and sound. After Effects or motion graphics experience is a plus.

  • You can direct people. You know how to make a nervous colleague relaxed on camera and how to interview to get a good answer.

  • You write. You can turn an interview or a product brief into a clear script.

  • You already use AI in your work — or you're curious and actively learning. Experience with AI video generation (e.g. Higgsfield, Runway, Kling, Veo, Sora) and AI-assisted editing is a strong plus.

  • You're proactive and independent. You see what needs doing, make the call, and get it done. You're comfortable working without close supervision and owning the outcome.

  • You understand performance content — what makes a viewer stop scrolling and how formats differ by channel.

  • Fluent in English. Danish is a plus.

  • Based in the Greater Copenhagen area.
